title: Curiosity Rover Finds “Sea of Polygons” on Martian Surface
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyCuriosity Rover Finds “Sea of Polygons” on Martian SurfaceIt’s not the first time the robot has found interesting patterns on the red planetJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CDT on July 30, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleSomeone’s going to be celebrating a birthday on Mars soon. On Aug. 6, 2012, NASA deployed the Curiosity rover to explore Gale Crater, and 14 years later, the birthday bot is still beaming back photos. The latest show striking honeycomb patterns in the Martian regolith that stretch as far as the electronic eye can see. Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 1016.3K 10Why We Haven't Found Life on Mars and Why Samples Must Return to EarthShareNextStayCURIOUS PATTERNS: A close-up of the honeycomb structures Curiosity discovered on Mars. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS.“We’ve seen a lot of fascinating landscapes through Curiosity’s eyes, but this sea of polygons took our breath away,” project scientist Ashwin Vasavada of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory said in a statement. “We measured their shapes and chemistry carefully and are hopeful there are clues in the data as to how these features formed.”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
